subject: general
question: How are Test cricket and ODIs contrasted in terms of viewer appeal?

options.text: Tests are faster and more entertaining
ODIs are only popular among senior fans
ODIs cater to shorter attention spans

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage notes that the "adrenaline-infused pace of ODIs appeals to a broader demographic, especially in an era of **dwindling attention spans** and time constraints."
 
• In contrast, Test cricket is described as a "slow-burning" format that requires "patience" and unfolds over five days, typically appealing to "purists."
 
• Therefore, the distinction in viewer appeal is that ODIs are designed for the modern viewer's need for faster, more compressed entertainment.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Relevant Quote:** *"The adrenaline-infused pace of ODIs appeals to a broader demographic, especially in an era of dwindling attention spans and time constraints."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** This is incorrect as the passage describes Test cricket as "slow-burning" and ODIs as the faster format.
 
• **Option 2:** The passage does not specify the age of fans, only that ODIs appeal to a "broader demographic."
 
• **Option 3:** This is incorrect; the passage states Test cricket rewards "consistency and grit" rather than just flamboyance/showmanship.
